title: Earlier owners of buildings the City bought or financed, in campaign and lobbying records
question: Do the organizations that held title before a City purchase, including the ones the Board file never names, appear as campaign donors or lobbyist clients?
finding: The index for 64 parcels names 76 organizations on a deed (banks, title companies, utilities, public bodies and private trusts left out). 12 of them also gave to a local campaign committee in their own name or hired a registered lobbyist; 10 are not in the earlier sellers-and-landlords screen, which read only the names in Board files. City Gardens 333 LLC (333 12th Street; 333-12th Street): 36 reported lobbying contacts, 2020-2021: 333 12th; 333 12th Street. Bodies contacted: Planning, Mayor, City Attorney. Personality Hotels LLC (440 Geary Street): 2 reported lobbying contacts, 2015-2015: Hotel Union Square Sign. Bodies contacted: City Planning. Chinatown Community Development Center (758 Pacific Avenue; 772+758 Pacific Ave; 777 Broadway Street, 1525 Grant Avenue, 1207 Mason Street): gave $215,635.
how: Every party to a document of type "deed" in the recorder's index printed for 64 deal parcels is taken as an organization in the chain of title; names that read as people or private trusts, public bodies, banks, title companies and utilities are dropped. Each name is searched, on the project name key, among contributions made in an organization's own name to local committees (schedules A and C), among clients in the lobbyist registry's reported contacts with officials, and in the Controller's payment file.
limits: Every row is a name match: these are single-purpose company names, most of them built from a street address, which makes a chance match unlikely but not impossible; the committee's filing or the lobbyist's registration gives the address that would confirm it. A donation to a ballot-measure committee, or hiring a lobbyist for a planning approval, is a permitted and common thing for a developer to do. The index gives no price. Deeds of trust, liens and leases are not used here; the “property records” analysis reads those.
